title: LUT-DLA: Lookup Table as Efficient Extreme Low-Bit Deep Learning Accelerator
problem: Scalar quantization cannot reduce DNN bit-width below 1-bit, capping compression gains; existing accelerators lack hardware support for vector-quantization-based LUT approaches that could push beyond this limit.
motivation: Growing DNN model sizes demand ever-lower inference costs, but the numerical floor of scalar quantization (1-bit) prevents further compression, necessitating vector quantization via lookup tables as a path to extreme low-bit inference.
method: LUT-DLA converts DNN weight tensors into lookup tables via vector quantization, replacing multiply-accumulate operations with LUT index lookups and accumulations. The LUTBoost algorithm trains DNNs through a multistage process to learn LUT-compatible vector codebooks. A co-design space exploration framework evaluates the trade-off between LUT table size, codebook dimensionality, model accuracy, and hardware cost to select optimal hardware configurations. The ASIC accelerator implements LUT fetch-and-accumulate dataflow units that directly consume quantized indices to perform inference.
key_novelty: Replacing conventional scalar MAC units with vector-quantization LUT fetch-and-accumulate hardware, achieving extreme sub-1-bit-equivalent compression through a hardware-algorithm co-design framework including the LUTBoost multistage training algorithm.
contributions: LUT-DLA accelerator framework enabling extreme low-bit DNN inference via vector quantization LUTs
LUTBoost multistage training algorithm to convert diverse DNN models into LUT-based representations
Co-design space exploration methodology linking model and hardware parameters for configuration tuning
1.4-7.0x power efficiency and 1.5-146.1x area efficiency improvements with modest accuracy drops (0.1-3.8% on CNNs, 1.4-3.0% on transformers)

metrics.accuracy: 0.1-3.8% accuracy drop on CNNs; 1.4-3.0% on transformers

limitations: Accuracy degradation of up to 3.8% on CNNs and 3.0% on transformers may be unacceptable for precision-sensitive tasks, and LUTBoost multistage training adds training complexity.
primary_theme: vector-quantization LUT accelerator for extreme low-bit DNN inference
